material_defects.name: ttl_cancel_before_tape_replay
material_defects.effect: an order older than the wall-clock TTL was deleted before newly received public trades were replayed, even when the trade event happened while the order was still live; delayed REST delivery could therefore create false zero-fills

material_defects.name: future_receive_not_explicitly_gated
material_defects.effect: the fill predicate required receive time after order creation but did not explicitly require receive time to be no later than the current processing instant

material_defects.name: fill_clock_assigned_to_processing_time
material_defects.effect: maker fills and position entry time were stamped at processing time instead of the public trade event time, biasing hold periods and post-fill markout timing

material_defects.name: missing_persistent_45_60_300_markout_watch
material_defects.effect: the V7 worker exited positions without retaining a dedicated watcher for executable 45s, 60s and 300s fill-conditioned markout evidence

repair_contract: local receive time remains the causal availability clock
market event time determines whether the trade occurred after simulated order arrival and before TTL expiry
newly known eligible trades are replayed before residual TTL/dead-queue cancellation
100ms simulated submit latency applies to both order arrival clocks
fill/position timing uses the public trade event timestamp
markout watchers survive position exit until 45s/60s/300s executable observations have been recorded
economic_interpretation: This repair can recover paper fills that were previously missed by bookkeeping, but it is not evidence of positive expected PnL. Promotion still requires chronological fill-conditioned PnL and adverse-selection markouts under normal and stressed costs.
